Dear Dana Whitfield,

Thank you for the discovery conversation of 6 October 2026. This letter proposes the Executive Briefing for Tamarack Instruments.

**Situation**

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. Its AI portfolio spans three stages:

- A customer service chatbot is deployed on the support portal.
- AI visual inspection is piloting on the German production line.
- AI sales forecasting is planned for next year.

Your stated objective is direct: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." The Client has named the EU AI Act and GDPR as regulatory drivers. It intends to begin ISO/IEC 42001 work next year, with the start date not yet fixed. It also requires customer data to stay in the EU and consults the German works council before anything touches production staff.

**What the Briefing Covers for Tamarack Instruments**

The session maps EU AI Act and GDPR expectations to each of the three use cases. This includes transparency expectations for the chatbot and how the visual inspection system should be classified before production. All regulatory points are framed as expectations to verify with counsel, not legal advice. United States requirements appear only as general landscape items, since none is named as a Client driver.

We test readiness against a Piloting maturity level. We also examine how the EU data residency constraint and works council consultation fit into a governance operating model built on two frameworks: the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) and Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen). AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards) serves as the board-layer reference.

We close on implementation priorities sequenced toward Q2 2027 and on how ISO/IEC 42001 preparation can build on that work. The Briefing does not promise certification, audit outcomes or regulatory approval. Throughout, we apply three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human.

**Logistics and Price**

The Briefing runs two hours, live virtual, for executive leadership and board-level attendees. Audience roles in scope are General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and two internal auditors. The price is US$3,000.

**What You Receive Afterward**

You will receive a follow-up memo recording decisions surfaced, readiness observations and three prioritized recommendations. Each recommendation is mapped to a next program option (Executive Workshop, Practitioner Academy or Implementation Accelerator) with a proposed timeline.

**Next Step**

Please reply to confirm the Briefing and propose session dates.

Kind regards,

Senior AI Governance Consultant
AI Governance Academy
